correctness.rationale: For 3∤n, any m=3 relation reduces to F(q)=0 mod e with F=1+X^a+X^b, 0≤a,b<n. A common complex root with X^n-1 requires two primitive cube roots, contradicting 3∤n; the nonzero resultant lies in the integral ideal and is divisible by e, and every factor of its n-root product has norm ≤3, proving e≤3^n. For 3|n, Phi_n divides 1+X^(n/3)+X^(2n/3). For sufficiently large q, Phi_n(q)>all nonzero resultants with X^d−1 for proper d|n, so the order mod Phi_n(q) is exactly n. Odd n disallows two-term zero sums by absence of -1 in odd-order subgroup. Even n is a multiple of 6: q≡1 mod3 gives Phi_n(q)≡1 mod3 and e=3Phi_n(q), preserving exact order n, allowing the three-term sum, and forbidding one or two terms modulo3. Phi_n(q) grows without bound. The packaged exact-arithmetic tests verify the representative finite computations, not the unrestricted quantifiers.

value.rationale: The function m(q,e)=3 is explicitly a published general open classification problem, and fixing multiplicative order is an intrinsic structural parameter. The result identifies a complete all-n sharp threshold for whether admissible moduli can be unbounded, gives a concrete 3^n bound in the finite regime, and an exact-order cyclotomic family including the even-order composite-modulus mechanism. This is an infinite structural theorem, not a routine single-parameter enumeration; it does not purport to solve the full classification.
